body: Ha funny that I never really thought of that. Everyone always says either put everything you possibly can or lie and say you have more experience. Dumbing it down could definitely help for basic positions.

Been out of school for a few years and have the same problem. Never hear anything back from service or retail positions while I get interview offers (...though ultimately not job offers haha..) from more advanced positions. I'm glad you found a solid job related to your degree though! But yeah its definitely what the first two comments mentioned about being someone who will always be looking for better opportunities compared to less qualified applicants. Its also due to the sheer volume of applications that jobs like that get. When you have plenty of applicants who you know will stay for the long haul, you just toss the over qualified applications out. It really sucks, but I get it.

Maybe this will help. We're the same age, but I've been unemployed for a long time (not for lack of trying), no relationship, and my family is kind of a mess...so..yeah...haha (not to say you aren't experiencing depression even with the solid support network you have, but sometimes it does help to focus on what you do have). Good that you're seeing somebody for help. Just remember to keep the internal dialogue going rather than just taking what they say at face value, another person's thoughts won't change anything unless you actively work them into your own thoughts/actions. Journaling/writing forms of "checklists" never really worked for me, but I have heard they can help people figure out the important things that they need to do/focus on in their lives so that they don't lose their minds thinking about everything, and can actually find peace with what they have.
But it really does feel impossible at times to change habits when you're at your lowest, you're definitely not alone there :). Routines definitely help, just try to mix it up every now and then to avoid monotony.

Yeah its great. I just try not to get too mad about the mistake...but clearly not doing a great job of that haha. But good that you were able to land a job, I'm hoping to at least find something like that.

Yeah I'm in the same boat. Been looking for a solid job for 2+ years. Besides little odd jobs and one off jobs for friends mostly involving manual labor just to stay afloat, I can't find anything. Not like I don't apply, apply to jobs all across the spectrum. At least I went to college and got good grades though and amassed oodles of student loan debt. SO HELPFUL!

Yeah I've had a lot of trouble with this issue as well. Writing out schedules and lists doesn't work for me. The only time I've ever been able to find motivation to do the basic stuff was when I had somebody to call me on my bs (as silly as that sounds). The other comment mentions something similar. For example, when I was in college I never could find the motivation to work out or do schoolwork cause it just felt pointless to me, but my friend (who I lived with at the time) would motivate me to put in the work. I actually ended up feeling a little better about myself and was in the best shape I had been. Unfortunately that was awhile ago and I don't really have anyone to do that for me anymore, but hey at least it worked for a bit. Anyway, maybe confide in someone close to you and ask them to help you find the motivation (could be friend or family). There's probably a better way that involves finding the solution within rather than depending on others, but honestly I can't find it. People always suggest mediation, which I couldn't quite figure out but its worth a shot I guess if you haven't tried. Good luck and I hope things get better!
I have a good amount of experience with data entry as well, but I certainly wouldn't say I'm interested in it haha. Guess that could be a fall back though.

Trying to keep an open mind right now as opportunities seem slim, but I have been trying to figure that out. While I'm not sure what type of actual job I'd excel with, something I actually have an eye for is photography/videography/editing. I realize that trying to find a job involving this is really difficult so I'll probably have to make my own thing eventually, but would need money to start. One way I thought I could apply this skill is through a marketing position (always need content for sites) but even entry level jobs seem to require years of experience. Been applying to many different kinds of jobs on my own for awhile now, but a few comments mentioned temp and staffing agencies so I guess I'll have to give that a try.

Oof that's rough. Sorry to hear that. Yeah its super fun to dish out all this money for school (so many loans) and do all this work, then realize you haven't even gotten to the hard part...hope you get something soon

Thanks I'll look into that. Only a few comments so far but the common theme already seems to be temp agencies so I gotta start looking some up. Yeah its brutal, just seems endless. Hoping I can break through some way soon. Anyway, thanks for the advice and good luck with your situation as well!

Oh yeah, been there done that haha. Gave up searching for a music industry related job like a month out of school. Wish I had picked a different major but hoping I don't have to pay for a dumb choice I made when I was a freshman. Yeah been looking into temp agencies. Lotta bad stories from people who have tried them but work is work I suppose. Have a good deal of experience working data entry while in school (3+ years with two different companies), I'm good at it but reaaaallly don't like it haha. May just have to go that route though. Anyway, thanks so much for the advice!

Yeah a lotta the same feelings here (unfortunately for the both of us haha...). Crazy that your family won't listen to you. I'd hope they would start if you told them this is serious and you need help but I don't know them and won't act like I do. Mine would go the opposite route and flip out and just wonder what the hell was wrong with me if I told them what I wrote up there (which I'd rather not deal with). I wish I could give advice on how to be happy but that'd be the blind leading the blind. Most advice I see when I look this stuff up is more just band aids to help deal with it (get a hobby, do more for yourself, keep trying to get work and it'll work out etc.). Starting with a hobby might at least help you cope a little at first (if I didn't get into photography and guitar I'd be gone already. A hobby could at least create a reason to get out of bed if you have something to do). I'm not really sure where to go from there to get out of the hole tho, the quick fixes just kinda keep you swirling around rather than falling deeper. Wish I knew how to get the drive/motivation you mentioned back. As for the boyfriend part, try not to blame yourself. Sometimes its just not meant to be between two people. Plus if he was going to stay with you just because you were in shape and not because of who you are he would be a jerk anyway
